title: Experiment Orbit: Cross-functional Rollout & Canary Ops (v0)
body:
Purpose:
Short: establish a compact, repeatable runbook and lightweight orchestration pattern for cross-functional LLM experiments that need staged exposure (smoke -> microcanary -> ramp) and A/B attribution without bloated ceremony. This is a working template (v0) intended for product + SRE + solutions + analytics collaboration.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: user-facing generation features, rerankers, and model variant switches (hosted & dedicated). Excludes infra-level kernel changes or hyperparameter-only research experiments.
- Audience: product owners, experiment owners, oncall SRE, analytics, solutions engineering.

High-level lifecycle (one-page checklist):
1) PLAN (D-14 to D-3)
   - Define hypothesis, primary metric, guardrail metrics, and success/fail thresholds.
   - Pick baseline cohort and treatment slices (min viable slices: 2 small synthetic + 1 production microcohort).
   - Create monitoring dashboard skeleton and synthetic traffic profile.
   - Stakeholder signoffs: product, privacy, legal if high-risk prompts.

2) SIMULATE (D-10 to D-2)
   - Run local/CI rollout-sim with production trace (sample N=50k requests) to estimate latency, token burn, failure modes.
   - Record tail latency distribution, cache hit-rate change, and expected cost delta.

3) DRY-RUN & SMOKE (D-2 to D)
   - Deploy to internal pilot namespace. Run smoke tests (canary-specific synthetic queries + golden prompt set).
   - Verify observability: llm_generation_latency_p95, model_error_rate_5xx, model_quality_regression_score.

4) MICROCANARY (D+0 to D+2)
   - Expose to 0.1%–1% of live traffic (microcohort). Short window (2–24h). Observe guardrails.
   - If any guardrail breaches, immediately rollback to baseline and trigger incident path.

5) RAMP & EXPAND (D+2 to D+7)
   - Incrementally increase exposure (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50%) with stability windows between steps (2–24h depending on risk).
   - Run A/B analysis at pre-agreed checkpoints. Check statistical power before big ramps.

6) FULL EXPOSURE / GRADUAL DECOMMISSION (post D+7)
   - Either promote to default route or decommission the experiment and archive artifacts.

7) RETROSPECT & ARTIFACT (D+14)
   - Post-mortem: hypothesis outcome, telemetry snapshot, cost delta, regressions, and lessons.

Roles & Responsibilities (quick matrix):
- Experiment Owner: drafts hypothesis, slice definitions, invites stakeholders. (Product / PM)
- Analytics: pre-compute power/sample size, set up metric queries and significance thresholds.
- Solutions Eng / Infra: ensures model variant routes, traffic partitioning, quotas, and fallback policies.
- SRE / Oncall: validates observability, configures alerts, owns rollback path.
- Legal / Privacy: approves dataset usage if prompts contain PII.

Guardrail metrics (examples & thresholds — tune per experiment):
- Latency: llm_generation_latency_p95 increase > 25% over baseline -> STOP.
- Errors: model_error_rate_5xx > 0.5% absolute increase -> STOP.
- Quality: model_quality_regression_score (eval set) drops by > 3 pts -> REVERT.
- Cost: per-token cost increase that would >10% exceed monthly budget forecast -> REVIEW.
- User-impact: critical user-path failure > 0.1% (e.g., broken checkout text) -> STOP.

Sampling & contamination handling:
- Use randomization at edge routing (flip-of-a-hash) to ensure deterministic allocation per user-id for multiday experiments.
- Avoid sampling users who previously saw other model-variant experiments in the last 14 days unless explicitly intended (tag in routing metadata).
- For candidate rerankers or multi-model flows, treat experiments as orthogonal only if they don't share downstream caches/state.

Microcohort selection heuristics (to surface early safety signals):
- Internal employees + power users (opt-in) + geographically small region (e.g., EU-west1) + low-value non-critical flows.
- Synthetic stress slice: intentionally noisy prompts to reveal hallucination or safety regressions.

Simulation checklist (quick):
- Input: 50k request traces (random 1% sample from production logs)
- Inject: golden prompt set (100 prompts) and 10% artificially malformed prompts
- Measure: latency tail, token distribution, KV cache hit-rate, prefix overlap, output-length distribution

Observability & dash requirements (must be live before canary):
- Time series: llm_generation_latency_{p50,p95,p99}, model_error_rate_4xx_5xx, token_burn_per_request, kv_cache_hit_rate
- Quality monitors: monthly eval dataset score, prompt-set drift index (similarity to training prompts)
- Cohort breakdown: metric by slice (region, plan, device, prior-experiment-tag)
- Alerts: auto-notify #experiment-orbit & oncall when guardrail threshold breached

Quick sample alert definitions (Prometheus/Alerts syntactic pseudo):
- ALERT CanaryHighP95 IF llm_generation_latency_p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.25 FOR 10m
- ALERT CanaryErrorSpike IF increase(model_error_rate_5xx, 5m) > 0.002 FOR 5m

Rollback & escape hatches (operational scripts):
- Fast rollback: change route weight to 0 for variant, promote baseline 100% (scripted terraform/feature-flag).
- Circuit break: auto-switch to smaller model variant or region-redundant route when capacity SLO violated.
- Oncall play: notify product, analytics, solutions, and CS. Create incident with severity tag and link to experiment id.

Comms snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- Slack (ops alert):
  "[EXPERIMENT-ORBIT] Canary breach: llm_generation_latency_p95 +28% vs baseline. Rolling back variant now. Experiment ID: E-2025-142. Oncall: @oncall. Notifying product & analytics."
- Customer-facing (if user impact):
  "We observed a regression in the new model and have reverted to the previous model while we investigate. Expected resolution: ETA 2–6 hours. Contact support@redwood.ai for urgent issues."

A/B analysis quick recipe:
- Pre-register primary metric and analysis plan (A/B waterfall: microcanary -> 2-way A/B -> multivariate if needed).
- Use blocked bootstrap or stratified t-test depending on metric distribution.
- Report both relative lift and absolute delta with 95% CI.

Data integrity checks pre/post-run:
- Ensure event ingestion completeness (requests vs impressions) - delta < 0.5%
- Check join keys (user_id, session_id) present for >99.5% of events
- Recompute a small-sample golden-set label agreement (manual) daily during rollout

Operational playbook (short runbook):
- 00:00 Start microcanary (0.1%) -> wait 3h -> check latency & errors -> signoff to 1%
- 03:00 1% -> wait 6h -> run quick statistical check -> signoff to 5%
- 12:00 5% -> wait 12h -> run full analytics snapshot -> decision to continue
- Any time: guardrail breach -> immediate rollback + post-incident runbook

Open questions & TODOs (notes-to-self):
- How to standardize model_quality_regression_score across different model types? (classification vs generation) -> TODO: propose normalized BLEU/ROUGE+human-calibration step.
- Decide canonical microcohort definition for PLG users vs enterprise customers.
- Investigate building an internal "rollout-sim" microservice to standardize simulations (github PR open).

Appendix: quick templates and links
- Experiment ID format suggestion: E-{YYYY}-{increment}
- Example JIRA template: JIRA-9982 (linked) includes hypothesis, slices, expected impact, dashboards
- Golden prompt set: link in confluence CONF-4821

End notes:
This is intentionally compact and operational. The goal is to reduce friction for small-to-medium risk LLM rollouts while preserving safety and cross-team clarity. Feedback welcome — add comments inline or ping in #experiment-orbit on Slack.

-- Aisha
